content: Last blind episode of this generation, and I should be honest about the situation: QED tops out near 0.89 and the SA term near 0.91 on this scaffold, so every small tweak I can make lands Phi within a few thousandths of 2.213. Three molecules are already tied there. Incremental cap and C4 swaps cannot break that - only jnk3 can, and it has been stuck at 0.41-0.43. So rather than bank another tie I will take the one combination with real upside. The two best single changes to the pyridine are a cyclopropyl at C4, which gave my highest activity at 0.43, and a methyl at C6, which I am testing separately this generation and which probes the far side of the ring nitrogen. Neither disturbs the bridging N-H or the ring nitrogen that the pharmacophore depends on, so if they act on different contacts they should add. Atom 15 is the cap cyclopropane CH bonded to the carbonyl at atom 13 over a non-ring bond, so I anchor there and hold the cap at cyclopropyl. The cost is mass: about 322 Da and LogP near 4.2 will pull QED to roughly 0.84, so this only wins if the two substituents genuinely combine - but if they do, generation 3 has ten episodes to exploit it.
